# KL divergence on held-out agents: ML models vs the P(flu) algorithm

<!-- Generated by ml/scripts/kl_summary.py from ml/results/kl/*_results.json; edit ml/scripts/kl_summary_head.md
     for this header. -->

How well does each model's P(infected during the run) match who actually got infected, on agents it never trained
on? Two 7,500-agent, 14-day runs, each scored on its own held-out 10%.

## Findings

- **`meanfield.js` was miscalibrated, not uninformative.** At its old defaults it predicted mean P ≈ 0.40 on runs
  where 4–11% got infected (per-agent KL 0.565 / 0.560, near the 0.693 of guessing 0.5). Two fixes bring it to
  0.178 / 0.303: start from the run's real prevalence (5 of 7,500, not 2% ≈ 150 phantom cases), and fit
  `lambdaScale` on the model as it is scored. Fitting it the `--calibrate` way (seeds, no reports) is not enough
  (0.325 / 0.545): the reports then add P on top of the spread the seeds already explain, ~4–5× too much.
- **frankenstein: the recalibrated `meanfield.js` is the best model**: per-agent KL 0.303 vs the MLP's 0.309 and a
  constant's 0.340, and the best ranking (AUC 0.689, AP 0.363). It fits one number; the MLP has 37k weights.
- **fixed: nothing beats a constant on KL.** `meanfield.js` (0.178), the GAT (0.178) and the constant (0.178) tie and
  the MLP is worse (0.188). `meanfield.js` still ranks best (AUC 0.63, AP 0.24 vs the MLP's 0.54 / 0.14). With 32
  infected validation agents these KL gaps are noise.
- **The simple GAT learned only the base rate** (AUC 0.53 / 0.54). Both runs capped its epochs for time, and on
  frankenstein its best epoch was the last, so it is under-trained, not ruled out.
- **Headroom.** An isotonic map from old-default `meanfield.js` to P, fitted on train labels, scores 0.163 / 0.301:
  `lambdaScale` fixes the level, but the spread of P is still off (calibration KL 0.0085 / 0.016).
- **The fitted `lambdaScale` tracks the sim.** frankenstein / fixed = 0.760 / 0.569 = 1.34 (with reports) and
  1.401 / 1.128 = 1.24 (`--calibrate`), vs the sim's transmission scales 1.446 / 1.2 = 1.21.

## Setup

- **Runs.** *fixed* (`influenza_none_n7500_d14_s42_9776284a`: old rule-based behaviour, sim transmission scale 1.2,
  5.3% infected) and *frankenstein* (`influenza_none_n7500_d14_s42_17ed9cd6`: behaviour calibrated from Claude-driven
  agents, scale 1.446, 10.3% infected). Both start from 5 seeds. See `sim/README.md`.
- **Split, per run.** The 7,495 non-seed agents are shuffled with `numpy.random.default_rng(0)` (as in
  `scripts/within_run.py`). Validation = the first 10% (750 agents). Of the rest, 10% (674) are a stop set for early
  stopping and model selection, and 6,071 are the fit set. "Train" = fit + stop (6,745). Ids:
  `results/kl/<run>_val_ids.json`. Seeds are never scored. Every model sees the whole run (all contacts, all agents);
  only the labels it learns from, or calibrates on, are restricted to train agents.
- **Label.** 1 if the agent was infected at any point in the run (any route).
- **Models.**
  - *MLP + ReLU* (`fluniml/mlp.py`, `full` features, mean of 3 seeds), fit on the fit set, early-stopped on the stop set.
  - *Simple GAT* (`fluniml/gat_daily.py`), loss on the fit set, checkpoint chosen on the stop set. Epochs were capped
    for time (~100 s each): fixed 20 with patience 8 (stopped at 13, best 5), frankenstein 12 (best was the last, so
    it is under-trained).
  - *`model/meanfield.js`* (Baker et al. mean field, phone inputs: contacts plus reports and tests). P = 1 − P(never
    infected) at the end of the run. Three versions:
    - **Fitted with reports** (the fair one): prior = 5/7,500 (the run's seed share, `initialPrevalence`) and one
      number, `lambdaScale`, fitted on the model as scored (reports included) so the mean P over train agents equals
      their attack rate (`scripts/kl_mf_fit.mjs`, 4 passes of ~20 min). **Fixed 0.569, frankenstein 0.760.**
    - **`--calibrate` fit**: same prior; `lambdaScale` fitted like `meanfield-cli.mjs --calibrate --holdout`: from the
      true seeds with no reports, expected on-campus infections = the train agents' count scaled to all non-seeds
      (fixed 364.5, frankenstein 718.9). **Fixed 1.128, frankenstein 1.401.** Then scored with reports.
    - **Old defaults**: prior 2%, `lambdaScale` 0.901 (fitted on a 1,000-agent run with 5% seeds).
  - `infer.js` and the Python `meanfield.py` were dropped from this comparison.
- **Baselines.** Constant P at the train rate; constant P at the validation rate (it cheats by knowing the answer's
  prevalence, so it is the best any constant can do); 0.5; and the truth (the floor).

## Metrics (nats, P clipped to [1e-6, 1 − 1e-6])

- **Per-agent KL** = mean over validation agents of KL(Bern(yᵢ) ‖ Bern(pᵢ)). Labels are 0/1, so this is the log loss.
  The headline number. A constant at the true rate scores H(ȳ): 0.176 on fixed, 0.340 on frankenstein.
- **Aggregate KL** = KL(Bern(ȳ) ‖ Bern(p̄)): is the overall rate right?
- **Calibration KL** = Σ over 10 equal-count bins of p (tied p share a bin) of (n_b/N)·KL(Bern(ȳ_b) ‖ Bern(p̄_b)). For a
  constant it equals the aggregate KL.
- AUC and average precision (AP) for ranking. With 32 (fixed) and 80 (frankenstein) infected validation agents,
  differences below ~0.01 nats or ~0.05 AUC are within noise.

## Reproduce

Large intermediate files go to `ml/out/kl/<run>/` (git-ignored, ~2–4 GB per run). Each run has its own scripts,
written in parallel for the two runs; they do the same steps.

```bash
# fixed
ml/.venv/bin/python ml/scripts/export_contacts_fixed.py sim/runs/influenza_none_n7500_d14_s42_9776284a ml/out/kl/fixed/contacts_bin
ml/.venv/bin/python ml/scripts/kl_fixed.py split            # then: mlp, gat --epochs 20 --patience 8
node --max-old-space-size=9000 ml/scripts/kl_fixed.mjs sim/runs/influenza_none_n7500_d14_s42_9776284a ml/out/kl/fixed/contacts_bin \
  meanfield ml/out/kl/fixed/meanfield_js_fixed_preds.csv     # also: meanfield_cal, meanfield_fit <target> <lo> <hi>
ml/.venv/bin/python ml/scripts/kl_fixed.py score            # -> ml/out/kl/fixed/results.json

# frankenstein
ml/.venv/bin/python ml/scripts/kl_frankenstein_prep.py && ml/.venv/bin/python ml/scripts/kl_frankenstein_export.py
ml/.venv/bin/python ml/scripts/kl_frankenstein.py split     # then: features, mlp, gat 12 12
node --max-old-space-size=10000 ml/scripts/kl_frankenstein.mjs meanfield   # also: meanfield_cal <target>, meanfield_fit <target> <lo> <hi>
ml/.venv/bin/python ml/scripts/kl_frankenstein.py score

python3 ml/scripts/kl_summary.py                            # this file + ml/results/kl/
```
